## Insights

**Starting point.** (1) Endpoint prediction and interior reconstruction provide different context. Explicit weighting makes their contributions controllable. (2) Averaging all masked positions gives examples with more targets greater influence. Per-example normalization removes that dependence. (3) The diagnosis describes excessive reliance on broad historical relevance. Endpoint supervision could improve next-choice alignment, but neither that feedback nor sampled margins establishes this effect.

**Related work.** (1) BERT4Rec already includes endpoint masking [1]. The proposed contribution is explicit supervision weighting, not a new masking mechanism. (2) Recency Sampling motivates investigating which historical prediction tasks receive training effort [2]. It does not establish that stronger endpoint weighting benefits these four datasets. (3) Sampled recommendation metrics can disagree with full-catalog rankings [3]. Selection must retain the pinned evaluator, while catalog diagnostics remain supporting evidence.

## Framework and directions

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed investigation |
|---|---|---|
| Objective alignment | Random and endpoint masking [1] | Explicit group-balanced loss |
| Temporal relevance | Recency sampling [2] | Recent versus older context ablation |
| Evaluation validity | Sampled ranking [3] | Fixed benchmark plus supporting catalog diagnostics |

## Candidate ideas

Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a benefit (+) and limitation (−).

1. **Balanced supervision: 4/7/2.** Originality: + explicit group normalization; − established masking modes. Potential: + inexpensive, interpretable experiment; − improvement is uncertain. Difficulty: + small loss change; − requires auditing target visibility and group membership.
2. **Recency-biased prefix endpoints: 4/6/3.** Originality: + combines prefix prediction with recency sampling [2]; − familiar sampling principle. Potential: + targets recent behavior; − may suppress persistent interests. Difficulty: + sampler-only modification; − changes the training-task distribution.
3. **Matched-context diagnostic: 3/6/3.** Originality: + controlled endpoint/interior comparison; − standard perturbation methodology. Potential: + tests dependence on right context; − does not itself improve recommendations. Difficulty: + reuses scoring; − careful target and candidate matching is necessary.

## Selected experiment: balanced supervision

At 10% progress, choose idea 1. Train one BERT4Rec per category with two explicitly sampled groups: endpoint-only masked prefixes and ordinary masked reconstruction. Hide every supervised target with the reserved MASK token. Average target cross-entropies within each example, average examples within each group, then optimize **0.5 × endpoint mean + 0.5 × reconstruction mean**. Equal example counts alone do not implement this objective when losses are pooled over tokens.

Keep architecture, optimizer, total batch size and training budget unchanged initially. Preserve seed 42, preprocessing seed 0, four-category routing, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Use appended-mask inference and the final nonpadding position. Preserve checkpoint/predictor consistency and diagnostic interfaces; add group-specific measured loss and margin summaries without claiming they predict HR@10.

Accept gains only through the fixed macro validation HR@10. No gains have yet been measured.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643; [3] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/

idea.description: Explicitly balance endpoint-only and ordinary masked-reconstruction supervision in each category’s single BERT4Rec model using equal group weights and per-example target normalization.
idea.motivation: Appended-mask inference lacks right context, while interior reconstruction can use it. A controlled weighting experiment tests whether allocating a fixed share of optimization to endpoint prediction improves the pinned validation objective.
idea.implementation_notes: Start from the supplied corrected baseline. Keep the BERT4Rec backbone and existing model/predictor serialization. Split the existing total batch size between two nonempty supervision groups. Construct endpoint examples exclusively from training-history prefixes, replacing the endpoint target with MASK; truncate earlier context to reserve room for that token. For reconstruction examples, replace every supervised position with MASK and never expose its target at that position. Compute catalog cross-entropy excluding PAD and MASK as output classes. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, four-category routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and all ModelView interfaces. Existing margins must use valid supervised MASK positions; unavailable measurements remain null. Each category loads exactly one trained checkpoint. Retain appended-mask inference with final-nonpadding readout. Select only by host macro validation HR@10; the weighting benefit is an untested hypothesis.
idea.pseudocode:
for category in four_categories:
    initialize_one_baseline_bert4rec(seed=42)
    for epoch in range(max_epochs_at_most_200):
        for step in range(200):
            endpoint = sample_training_prefixes(endpoint_group_size)
            endpoint_inputs, endpoint_targets = mask_last_real_item(endpoint)
            reconstruction = sample_training_sequences(reconstruction_group_size)
            reconstruction_inputs, reconstruction_targets = mask_selected_targets(reconstruction)
            assert_all_supervised_inputs_are_reserved_MASK()
            endpoint_losses = cross_entropy_at_supervised_positions(model(endpoint_inputs), endpoint_targets)
            reconstruction_losses = cross_entropy_at_supervised_positions(model(reconstruction_inputs), reconstruction_targets)
            endpoint_mean = mean(per_example_mean(endpoint_losses))
            reconstruction_mean = mean(per_example_mean(reconstruction_losses))
            loss = 0.5 * endpoint_mean + 0.5 * reconstruction_mean
            optimizer.zero_grad()
            loss.backward()
            optimizer.step()
    save_single_category_checkpoint_and_matching_predictor()
# Inference: left-pad retained history plus appended MASK;
# score from the final nonpadding position using that category's one model.

originality.positive: Explicit group weighting and per-example normalization make the allocation of supervision independently controllable.
originality.negative: Both endpoint masking and random masked reconstruction are existing BERT4Rec mechanisms.

future_potential.positive: Provides a simple experiment for studying how training-task allocation affects next-item prediction.
future_potential.negative: Equal weighting is heuristic, and improved objective alignment may not improve validation ranking.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a small sampler and loss-reduction change without adding an inference component.
code_difficulty.negative: Incorrect target hiding or token-level reduction could silently invalidate the experiment.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation.
Includes endpoint masking to support next-item prediction.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed equal group weighting improves this benchmark.
Interior reconstruction can exploit right context unavailable during appended-mask inference.

related_work.title: Recency Sampling for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Motivates controlling the temporal distribution of sequential recommendation training tasks.
limitations: Does not directly validate explicit endpoint-versus-reconstruction loss weighting on the four prescribed categories.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Establishes that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog metrics and reverse model comparisons.
limitations: Does not identify an optimal BERT4Rec training objective.
Its findings do not authorize changing the pinned benchmark selection criterion.
